```text
1	# Agent Firehose
2	
3	A local-first developer tool that shows a live, structured timeline of what AI
4	coding agents are doing on your Mac. Like a Twitter firehose, but for agent
5	activity: fast, scrollable, information-dense, readable.
6	
7	```
8	AGENT FIREHOSE  ● LIVE  1,204 events
9	10:04:12 │ [claude]   [prompt]     prompt: "fix the login bug"            …/dev/app
10	10:04:15 │ [claude]   [shell]      ran: go test ./...                     …/dev/app
11	10:04:19 │ [codex]    [file]       patched router.ex, health.ex           …/dev/api
12	10:04:20 │ [opencode] [permission] permission requested: Run: rm -rf build
13	10:04:21 │ [claude]   [file]       ran Edit on auth.go ×3                 …/dev/app
14	space pause · ↑/↓ scroll · enter detail · f category · a source · / search · t density · e export · q quit
15	```
16	
17	Everything runs on-device. No backend, no accounts, no sync, no telemetry.
18	
19	## Install
20	
21	```sh
22	go install agentfirehose/cmd/firehose@latest   # or: git clone && go build ./cmd/firehose
23	```
24	
25	Put the `firehose` binary on your `PATH`, then wire up the agents you use:
26	
27	```sh
28	firehose install claude-code   # merges hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json (backs it up first)
29	firehose install opencode      # writes a plugin into ~/.config/opencode/plugin/
30	firehose doctor                # verify everything is wired
31	firehose                       # open the live view
32	```
33	
34	Codex needs no install step — the engine tails `~/.codex/sessions` directly.
35	
36	## The daemon
37	
38	The capture engine can run as a long-lived local daemon that owns the spool
39	and serves a localhost API (default `127.0.0.1:4517`):
40	
41	```sh
42	firehose daemon            # run the engine: watchers, spool writes, local API
43	firehosed                  # same engine as a dedicated binary (used as the desktop sidecar)
44	firehose status            # is it running? which version/schema?
45	```
46	
47	When the daemon is running, `firehose emit` (and every installed adapter)
48	routes payloads through it, and the TUI consumes its live stream instead of
49	tailing files itself. When it isn't, everything falls back to direct spool
50	access — capture never depends on the daemon being up. The API surface
51	(events, live SSE stream, sessions, doctor, export) is documented in
52	[docs/contracts.md](docs/contracts.md).
53	
54	## The desktop app
55	
56	A Tauri shell in [apps/tauri-desktop](apps/tauri-desktop) wraps the engine
57	for non-terminal users: live feed, session explorer, touched-file view,
58	doctor with one-click adapter install, settings, and a first-run onboarding
59	wizard. It bundles `firehosed` as a sidecar and spawns it when no daemon is
60	already running — a daemon you run yourself always wins.
61	
62	```sh
63	scripts/build-sidecar.sh                    # compile firehosed into the sidecar slot
64	pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop install
65	pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop tauri dev        # develop
66	pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop tauri build      # package (.app / .msi / AppImage)
67	```
68	
69	Packaging for macOS, Windows, and Linux is validated in CI
70	([desktop workflow](.github/workflows/desktop.yml)); signing and the update
71	feed are documented in the [release runbook](docs/release-runbook.md).
72	
73	## Supported sources
74	
75	| Source | Depth | How it works |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| Claude Code | deep | hooks forward every lifecycle event to `firehose emit` |
78	| Codex | deep | viewer tails rollout session JSONL files |
79	| OpenCode | deep | plugin forwards bus events to `firehose emit` |
80	| any process | shallow | process watcher emits start/stop for known agent binaries |
81	| anything else | generic | pipe NDJSON into `firehose ingest`, or call `firehose emit` |
82	
83	## The viewer
84	
85	- **live mode** pins to the bottom; `space` pauses and counts unread events
86	- `f` cycles category filter (session/prompt/message/tool/file/permission/shell/error/meta)
87	- `a` cycles source filter, `/` searches summaries
88	- `enter` opens a detail pane with the full structured payload
89	- `t` toggles compact density, `e` exports the current view to NDJSON
90	- bursty repeats coalesce into one row with a `×N` counter
91	- adapter failures and unparseable lines surface *in the timeline* as `meta/warn` events
92	
93	## Privacy modes
94	
95	Set in `~/.agentfirehose/config.json` (`{"privacy_mode": "balanced"}`):
96	
97	- `minimal` — payload values stored as `{sha256, len}` digests only
98	- `balanced` (default) — payload strings truncated to 240 chars, raw payloads dropped
99	- `full` — everything, including raw source payloads
100	
101	Captured events live in `~/.agentfirehose/spool/*.ndjson`. Delete the
102	directory to delete your history.
103	
104	## Export
105	
106	```sh
107	firehose export -o events.ndjson    # everything captured
108	```
109	
110	Or press `e` in the viewer to export exactly what you're looking at
111	(filters applied).
112	
113	## Docs
114	
115	- [Platform contract](docs/contracts.md) — frozen surfaces: envelope schema, spool/export formats, privacy semantics, local API
116	- [Event schema](docs/event.schema.json) — JSON Schema for the normalized envelope
117	- [Adapter guide](docs/adapters.md) — how each adapter works and how to add one
118	- [Migration plan](docs/agent-firehose-migration-plan.md) — daemon → desktop shell → optional cloud (with status)
119	- [Compatibility](docs/compatibility.md) — daemon/UI schema-version rules
120	- [Release runbook](docs/release-runbook.md) — signing, packaging, updater feed
121	- [Pain review](docs/migration/pain-review.md) — Phase 4 engine decision framework
122	- [Cloud control plane](docs/architecture/cloud-control-plane.md) — Phase 5 design (deferred)
123	- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
124	
125	## License
126	
127	MIT
128

1	# AGENTS.md — Lattice
2	
3	Least-authority process plane on the BEAM (V1, proven) + durable self-certifying Replica substrate (2.0). Core thesis: zero implicit authority; the log is the truth; the connection is the cache.
4	
5	**State:** branch `claude/beautiful-gould-6b25d2` — M1 (Lattice 2.0 core) is GREEN: all 19 behaviors, 9 properties/67 tests across seeds 1/7/99/555/2024/12345, demo narrates. Current work: M1 close-out (countersign, D-A1 agility note, merge proposal) and M2 (carrier) per `docs/agent/register.md` W-series.
6	
7	**Before any work: read `docs/agent/HANDOFF.md`; confirm `docs/agent/reconciliation_report.md` §5 is countersigned for your tree.**
8	
9	## Commands
10	```
11	mix deps.get
12	mix format --check-formatted
13	mix test                              # expect 0 failures, 0 skipped
14	mix run scripts/lattice2_demo.exs     # 2.0 narrated demo (also: elixir scripts/lattice2_demo.exs)
15	scripts/lattice_poc_demo.sh           # V1 demo
16	mix lattice.stress --tabs 500 --caps 2000 --calls 50000 --bridges 1000
17	npm install && npm run browser:e2e    # Playwright evidence
18	mix lattice.browser_carrier.proof     # carrier spike proof artifact
19	```
20	Validation loop (never weaken without human sign-off): `mix format` → `mix test` → `mix run scripts/lattice2_demo.exs`. Carrier work adds the conformance oracle: real carrier ≡ `Lattice.Sim` final logs/state for the same op set.
21	
22	## Hard rules
23	- Toolchain: Elixir on **OTP 28** (ADR 0001 verifies `:deterministic` there). Core = plain OTP. Dep whitelist: `cowboy`, `jason` (boundary), `stream_data` (test), `@playwright/test` (e2e). **New dep = escalate.**
24	- DO NOT IMPLEMENT (full list HANDOFF §3): encryption, key rotation, recovery, ZKP/accumulators, consensus, receipt-freeness machinery, full compaction, PQC code, DID registries, federation. Seeming necessary → question the requirement, escalate.
25	- Canonical encoding is ADR 0001's pinned `term_to_binary [:deterministic, minor_version: 2]`; the CBOR migration is ADR-P08 — an ADR'd migration with golden vectors, never a hot swap.
26	- No wall clocks in semantics (`Lattice.Clock` only; ticks in op bodies — invariant 5). No folds over bare maps in reduce/merge/authority paths.
27	- All authority verdicts flow through `Authority.analyze/2`; `Live.authorize/2` consults the same in-log revokes. No second path.
28	- Non-holder writes to authoritative fields use the inbox `:request` pattern (behavior 6). Do not rebind v1 facade names (`Lattice.call/grant/cast`).
29	- Tests are the spec: failing test first; never edit expectations to match code; no `@tag :skip`/pending. Property generators are never narrowed.
30	- Every merge appends a status-doc line (`docs/agent/status_protocol.md`); failing seeds logged with shrunk case before the fix. Commits name the behavior/ADR (`B16: …` / `ADR-P08: …`). Merges to `main` are human-approved.
31	
32	## Escalate to the human when
33	Crypto choices/deviations · new deps · reinterpreting a behavior's meaning · anything touching `author`/identity/rotation · coordinator-shaped singletons · a boundary item seeming necessary · weakening a property/generator · a seed-fix that would change a ratified ADR · two consecutive failed gate attempts · any merge/publish to `main`.
34	
35	## Vocabulary
36	Use HANDOFF §10 verbatim (op, deps, Replica, materialization, reduction, holder, delegation, Cap, quarantine reasons, tick, heartbeat, frontier, oracle). No synonyms.
37
```

```text
1	# Contributing
2	
3	Agent Firehose is a small, local-first Go project. Contributions that add
4	adapters, improve timeline readability, or harden capture paths are the most
5	valuable.
6	
7	## Ground rules
8	
9	- **TDD.** Every behavior change starts with a failing test. The test suite is
10	  fast (`go test ./...` runs in seconds) — keep it that way.
11	- **Local-first.** No network calls, no telemetry, no cloud dependencies.
12	- **Structured over verbose.** Every event needs a category, a one-line human
13	  summary, and enough payload to understand it in the detail pane.
14	- **Never break the agent.** Capture paths (hooks, plugins) must fail silently
15	  rather than interrupt someone's coding session. Surface failures in the
16	  timeline instead (`meta`/`warn` events).
17	
18	## Development
19	
20	```sh
21	go test ./...          # full suite
22	go vet ./...
23	go build ./cmd/firehose
24	```
25	
26	Package layout:
27	
28	- `internal/event` — the normalized envelope (start here)
29	- `internal/privacy` — capture-mode redaction
30	- `internal/spool` — NDJSON persistence + tailing
31	- `internal/adapters/*` — one package per source
32	- `internal/store` — ring buffer, filters, coalescing
33	- `internal/tui` — Bubble Tea model/view
34	- `internal/cli` — testable subcommand implementations
35	- `cmd/firehose` — flag parsing and wiring only
36	
37	## Adding an adapter
38	
39	See [docs/adapters.md](docs/adapters.md). Start from real captured payloads —
40	paste actual lines from the source into your parser tests as fixtures rather
41	than inventing shapes.
42	
43	## Pull requests
44	
45	Keep them focused. A PR that adds one adapter with tests and a doctor check is
46	ideal. Include a sample of the raw source payloads your parser handles.
47
```
</details></tool-use>

141	// runDaemon runs the capture engine and its local API until interrupted.
142	func runDaemon(cfg cfgType, home, addr string) error {
143		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
144		defer stop()
145	
146		return daemon.Run(ctx, cfg, home, version, addr, func(bound string) {
147			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "firehose daemon listening on %s (spool: %s)\n", bound, cfg.SpoolDir)
148		})
149	}
150	
151	// runView opens the TUI. When a daemon is running it is the single source of
152	// events; otherwise the viewer falls back to capturing directly.
153	func runView(cfg cfgType) error {
154		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
155		defer cancel()
156	
157		events, history, err := viewFeed(ctx, cfg)
158		if err != nil {
159			return err
160		}
161	
162		model := tui.NewModel(events)
163		model = model.Preload(history)
164		model.ExportFn = func(evs []event.Event) (string, error) {
165			name := fmt.Sprintf("firehose-export-%s.ndjson", time.Now().Format("20060102-150405"))
166			f, err := os.Create(name)
167			if err != nil {
168				return "", err
169			}
170			defer f.Close()
171			for _, ev := range evs {
172				data, err := jsonLine(ev)
173				if err != nil {
174					return "", err
175				}
176				if _, err := f.Write(data); err != nil {
177					return "", err
178				}
179			}
180			return name, nil
181		}
182	
183		_, err = tea.NewProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen()).Run()
184		return err
185	}
186	
187	// viewFeed prefers the daemon's stream; without one it merges the spool
188	// tailer, codex session watcher, and process watcher locally.
189	func viewFeed(ctx context.Context, cfg cfgType) (<-chan event.Event, []event.Event, error) {
190		if cfg.DaemonAddr != "" {
191			c := client.New("http://" + cfg.DaemonAddr)
192			if _, err := c.Health(); err == nil {
193				stream, err := c.Stream(ctx)
194				if err != nil {
195					return nil, nil, err
196				}
197				history, err := c.Recent(500)
198				if err != nil {
199					return nil, nil, err
200				}
201				return stream, history, nil
202			}
203		}
204	
205		mode, err := privacy.ParseMode(cfg.PrivacyMode)
206		if err != nil {
207			mode = privacy.ModeBalanced
208		}
209		raw := make(chan event.Event, 1024)
210		go spool.NewTailer(cfg.SpoolDir, 100*time.Millisecond).Run(ctx, raw)
211		if _, err := os.Stat(cfg.CodexDir); err == nil {
212			go codex.NewWatcher(cfg.CodexDir, 250*time.Millisecond).Run(ctx, raw)
213		}
214		go procwatch.NewWatcher(procwatch.PSLister{}, 2*time.Second).Run(ctx, raw)
215	
216		// Codex events are read straight from its files, so redact here; spooled
217		// events were already redacted at append time.
218		events := make(chan event.Event, 1024)
219		go func() {
220			for {
221				select {
222				case <-ctx.Done():
223					return
224				case ev := <-raw:
225					if ev.Source == codex.Source {
226						ev = privacy.Redact(ev, mode)
227					}
228					select {
229					case events <- ev:
230					case <-ctx.Done():
231						return
232					}
233				}
234			}
235		}()
236		history, _ := spool.ReadLastN(cfg.SpoolDir, 500)
237		return events, history, nil
238	}

244		if err != nil {

246		}
247		return append(data, '\n'), nil
248	}

```text
1	# Platform contract
2	
3	This document freezes the compatibility boundary of Agent Firehose (migration
4	plan, Phase 0). Adapters, spool data, exports, and clients built against these
5	contracts must keep working as the UI evolves. Changing anything here requires
6	a version bump and a documented migration.
7	
8	The five frozen surfaces:
9	
10	1. **Event envelope schema** — [`event.schema.json`](event.schema.json)
11	2. **Privacy mode semantics** — below
12	3. **NDJSON spool format** — below
13	4. **Export format** — below
14	5. **Local API** — below
15	
16	## Event envelope (`schema_version`)
17	
18	Every captured event is normalized into the envelope defined in
19	[`event.schema.json`](event.schema.json). The current `schema_version` is
20	**1** (`event.CurrentSchemaVersion`).
21	
22	Evolution rules:
23	
24	- New optional fields may be added without bumping the version. Consumers
25	  MUST ignore unknown fields. (Example: `trace_id` — optional, groups
26	  causally related events across sessions when a source supplies one —
27	  was added additively within version 1.)
28	- Removing, renaming, or changing the meaning of a field requires a version
29	  bump and a reader that understands both versions.
30	- Spool lines written before versioning have no `schema_version` field;
31	  readers treat absent/`0` as version 1.
32	
33	## Privacy modes
34	
35	Redaction happens **before persistence** — the spool never contains more than
36	the configured mode allows. The mode is applied at the engine boundary: at
37	spool-append time for emitted/ingested events, and at broadcast time for
38	events read directly from other tools' files (codex).
39	
40	| Mode | `raw` | `payload` values | Metadata (source, category, name, times, ids, repo/cwd, summary) |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| `minimal` | dropped | replaced with `{"sha256": "...", "len": N}` digests | kept |
43	| `balanced` (default) | dropped | strings truncated to 240 runes (with `…`) | kept |
44	| `full` | kept | kept verbatim | kept |
45	
46	## Spool format
47	
48	- Location: `spool_dir` (default `~/.agentfirehose/spool`).
49	- One file per UTC day, named `YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson`; files sort chronologically.
50	- Each line is one JSON event envelope; writers append whole lines with
51	  `O_APPEND` so concurrent producers never interleave.
52	- The spool is the canonical, append-only source of truth. Derived stores
53	  (indexes, caches) must be rebuildable from it.
54	- Readers skip unparseable lines; the tailer surfaces them as `meta`/`warn`
55	  events instead of failing.
56	
57	## Export format (`export_version`)
58	
59	`export_version` **1** (`cli.ExportVersion`) is NDJSON of schema-versioned
60	event envelopes, one per line, oldest first — the spool format, concatenated
```

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> Note: `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agent/` in this repo describe an unrelated Elixir project
> ("Lattice") and were copied in by mistake. Ignore them. This is **Agent Firehose**,
> a Go project. There is no `mix` project here.

## What this is

Agent Firehose is a local-first developer tool that shows a live, structured timeline of
what AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, …) are doing on your machine — a
Bubble Tea TUI over an on-device capture engine. Everything runs on-device: no backend,
no accounts, no sync, no telemetry. A Tauri v2 desktop shell (`apps/tauri-desktop`) wraps
the same engine for non-terminal users.

## Commands

\```sh
go test ./...                         # full suite (fast — keep it that way)
go test ./internal/adapters/codex     # single package
go test -run TestName ./internal/tui  # single test
go vet ./...
gofmt -l .                            # list unformatted files (must be empty)
go build ./cmd/firehose               # the CLI+TUI binary
go build ./cmd/firehosed              # the dedicated daemon binary (desktop sidecar)
\```

Validation loop before marking work complete: `gofmt -l .` → `go vet ./...` → `go test ./...`.

Desktop app (`apps/tauri-desktop`, uses **pnpm**):

\```sh
scripts/build-sidecar.sh                    # compile firehosed into the sidecar slot first
pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop install
pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop test             # vitest (frontend state/client)
pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop build            # tsc + vite build
pnpm -C apps/tauri-desktop tauri dev        # run the shell
cargo test --manifest-path apps/tauri-desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml   # Rust side
\```

If `pnpm`/`node`/`npx` misbehave in a non-interactive shell, they are shadowed by an nvm
shim — prefix with `PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin:$PATH` or run `unfunction node npm npx`.

Running the tool live: `firehose install claude-code` merges hooks into
`~/.claude/settings.json`; captured events land in `~/.agentfirehose/spool/*.ndjson`; a
daemon on `127.0.0.1:4517` serves the live API.

## Architecture

Everything funnels through **one normalized envelope** (`internal/event`, `event.Event`).
Every capture source is mapped into it before display, persistence, or export. Start there
when learning the codebase.

Data flow:

\```
sources ──adapters──▶ event.Event ──privacy.Redact──▶ spool (NDJSON) ──▶ store/index ──▶ TUI / API
\```

- **`internal/event`** — the `Event` envelope + `CurrentSchemaVersion` (currently 1). The
  frozen contract; new fields must be additive (see below).
- **`internal/adapters/*`** — one package per source, each mapping raw payloads into
  `Event`s. `claudecode` & `opencode` receive pushed payloads via `firehose emit`; `codex`
  *tails* `~/.codex/sessions` JSONL directly; `procwatch` polls the process list for known
  agent binaries; `generic` handles arbitrary NDJSON via `firehose ingest`.
- **`internal/privacy`** — redaction applied **before persistence**, at the engine boundary.
  Modes: `minimal` (values → `{sha256,len}`), `balanced` default (strings truncated to 240
  runes, `raw` dropped), `full`. The spool never holds more than the mode allows.
- **`internal/spool`** — append-only NDJSON, one file per UTC day (`YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson`),
  `O_APPEND` so concurrent producers never interleave. **This is the canonical source of
  truth**; every derived store must be rebuildable from it. Also provides the tailer.
- **`internal/index`** — derived in-memory index (sessions/traces/artifacts) built over the
  spool; powers the daemon's query endpoints.
- **`internal/store`** — ring buffer, filters, and burst coalescing (`×N` rows) for the TUI.
- **`internal/daemon`** — the capture engine as a long-lived local API (`net/http`
  `mux.HandleFunc`, Go 1.22+ routing). Routes: `/health`, `/config`, `/events`,
  `/events/stream` (SSE), `/emit`, `/sessions[/{id}]`, `/traces/{id}`, `/artifacts/files`,
  `/doctor`, `/install/{adapter}`, `/export`.
- **`internal/client`** — HTTP client the TUI/desktop use to consume the daemon.
- **`internal/tui`** — Bubble Tea model (`tui.go`) + rendering (`view.go`).
- **`internal/cli`** — testable subcommand implementations (config, doctor, install, status,
  emit, ingest, export). `cmd/firehose/main.go` is flag parsing + wiring only.

**Daemon-optional design (important):** capture NEVER depends on the daemon being up. When
a daemon is running, `firehose emit` and adapters route through it and the TUI consumes its
stream (`viewFeed` in `cmd/firehose/main.go` prefers the daemon). When it isn't, everything
falls back to direct spool access — the TUI merges the spool tailer, codex watcher, and
procwatch locally. A daemon the user runs themselves always wins over the desktop sidecar.

## Hard rules (from CONTRIBUTING.md and the frozen contract)

- **TDD.** Every behavior change starts with a failing test. For adapters, use *real
  captured payloads* pasted from the source as fixtures — never invent shapes.
- **Local-first.** No network calls, no telemetry, no cloud dependencies.
- **Never break the agent.** Capture paths (hooks, plugins) must fail *silently* rather than
  interrupt a coding session — surface failures *in the timeline* as `meta`/`warn` events.
- **The five frozen surfaces** (`docs/contracts.md`): event envelope schema, privacy
  semantics, NDJSON spool format, export format, local API. Adding an optional field is fine
  and needs no version bump (consumers ignore unknown fields). **Removing/renaming/changing
  the meaning of a field, or changing privacy/spool/export/API semantics, requires a
  `schema_version` bump + a reader that understands both versions** — escalate.
- **Dependencies are minimal** (Bubble Tea + Lipgloss, std lib otherwise). Adding a Go dep is
  a deliberate choice — prefer the standard library.
- Merges to `main` are human-approved.

## Docs worth reading

`docs/contracts.md` (frozen surfaces), `docs/event.schema.json` (envelope JSON Schema),
`docs/adapters.md` (how each adapter works / how to add one),
`docs/agent-firehose-migration-plan.md` (daemon → desktop → optional cloud; status at top —
phases 0–3 done, 4–5 gated), `docs/compatibility.md`, `docs/release-runbook.md`.

# ADR-P08 — Language-neutral wire format: canonical CBOR (closes W-01)
## Status
PROPOSED.
## Context
ADR 0001 pins `term_to_binary [:deterministic, minor_version: 2]` and honestly names its limits: BEAM-specific, atoms-vs-binaries distinct, no cross-runtime guarantee. `path_to_real.md` §1 designates canonical CBOR as the wire format so a JS/AtomVM/Rust peer hashes and verifies identically. This ADR is the migration design; it must not change any behavior's semantics.
## Decision
Ops and delegations encode as **RFC 8949 core-deterministic CBOR, positional arrays** (no maps at the top level): `[version, replica, author, deps_sorted, kind, body, cap]` with a schema registry pinning every `kind`/`body` shape (atoms encode as pinned small-int enum or text — one choice, documented, forever). `id = sha256(cbor)`, url-safe base64 unpadded, as today. Migration is **dual-encode**: for a transition window every op encodes both ways in tests, asserting equal semantic content and stable ids per format; the log stores ids under one format version tag. Golden vectors (bytes + ids) are committed and CI-checked.
## Alternatives considered

=== ADR-P10 head ===
# ADR-P10 — Heartbeats derived from carrier liveness (closes W-03, ADR 0004 caveat)
## Status
PROPOSED.
## Context
ADR 0004: dormancy = absence of heartbeats, POC emits them explicitly for deterministic windows, and names the production fix — derive heartbeats from connection liveness on the carrier. The trap: importing wall-clock or connection state into reduction would break invariant 5.
## Decision
The **boundary authors ops; reduction stays pure.** The carrier (per ADR-P09) observes liveness (socket up, pings) and, on a policy cadence, authors ordinary `{:heartbeat, role, at_tick}` ops on the holder's behalf-of-itself (holder-signed at the client), with `at_tick` drawn from the same explicit logical clock ops already carry. Reduction/validation are untouched — a carrier-driven heartbeat is indistinguishable in-log from an explicit one (same ADR 0004 validity rule: authored by holder-at-its-deps). The deterministic suite keeps emitting explicit heartbeats; carrier tests assert only that liveness produces well-formed heartbeat ops at the boundary.
## Alternatives considered

# Agent Firehose Migration Plan

## Status (2026-07-06)

| Phase | State |
|---|---|
| Phase 0 — platform contract freeze | **Done** — [contracts.md](contracts.md), [event.schema.json](event.schema.json), schema/export versioning |
| Phase 1 — engine/clients split | **Done** — daemon + full local API (incl. `POST /config`, `/traces/{id}`, `/artifacts/files`, `POST /install/{adapter}`), `firehosed` binary, TUI/CLI route through the daemon, `trace_id` in the envelope |
| Phase 2 — derived index over NDJSON | **Done** — in-memory index (`internal/index`) rebuilt from the spool at startup, updated from the tail; spool remains source of truth. bbolt/SQLite remains the documented next step if RAM ever hurts |
| Phase 3 — Tauri desktop shell | **Done (alpha)** — [apps/tauri-desktop](../apps/tauri-desktop): live feed, sessions, files, doctor + install, settings, onboarding, compat banner; `firehosed` sidecar; macOS bundle validated locally, Windows/Linux in [CI](../.github/workflows/desktop.yml); signing/updater are human-credential steps in the [release runbook](release-runbook.md) |
| Phase 4 — keep/replace decision | **Framework ready** — [migration/pain-review.md](migration/pain-review.md); fill after real beta usage, per this plan's own exit criteria |
| Phase 5 — Phoenix cloud | **Design only, deferred** — [architecture/cloud-control-plane.md](architecture/cloud-control-plane.md); gated by this plan's anti-goals |

Deviations from the letter of this plan (with rationale) are recorded in
[plans/2026-07-06-daemon-desktop-migration.md](plans/2026-07-06-daemon-desktop-migration.md).

## Goal

Evolve the current local-first Go TUI into a distributable cross-platform desktop product in three stages:

1. **Current state:** Go CLI/TUI + local adapters + NDJSON spool.
2. **Next state:** Go daemon + Tauri desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
3. **Optional future state:** Phoenix cloud backend for sync, fleet analytics, collaboration, and hosted observability.

The key principle is to preserve the current event model and spool/export contract as the durable platform boundary rather than rebuilding the entire system immediately.[cite:66]

## Why this path

The current implementation already has the right product core: a normalized `Event` envelope, adapter-driven ingestion, privacy redaction before persistence, local NDJSON spool files, export, install/doctor commands, and a viewer that can tail live activity.[cite:66]

That means the risky and product-defining work is largely done already. The missing layer is a better desktop packaging and visualization story for non-TUI users, not a new ingestion model.[cite:66]

Tauri is a strong fit for the desktop shell because it is designed for small, secure cross-platform desktop apps with a web frontend and Rust backend, and it supports updater workflows for macOS, Windows, and Linux distributions.[cite:72][cite:68][cite:75]

Phoenix should be treated as an optional later control plane, not as the local desktop runtime. It is most valuable if the product grows into shared dashboards, team views, remote ingestion, or cloud-hosted observability.[cite:66]

## Architectural north star
